title: Why Lime and Onion Works So Well Together
flavorProfile: The union of lime and onion is a masterclass in balancing sharp acidity with pungent sulfurous heat. Lime provides high citric acid content that cuts through the heavy, allium-based richness of onions, while the onion's natural sugars and quercetin offer a savory backbone that prevents the lime from tasting one-dimensional. This pairing creates a bright, zesty, and slightly bitter profile that enhances umami in proteins and freshens up starchy bases, making it a cornerstone of global cuisines from Mexican salsas to Indian chutneys.
nutritionalSynergy: Combining lime and onion enhances the bioavailability of quercetin, a flavonoid found in onions, due to the acidic environment created by the lime. This synergy also boosts the absorption of vitamin C from the lime, which acts as a powerful antioxidant. Together, they provide a potent anti-inflammatory effect, supporting cardiovascular health and immune function through the combined action of sulfur compounds and citric acid.
prepTechniques: Dice the onion finely and marinate it in lime juice for 15 minutes to mellow the raw pungency and create a translucent, tender texture.
Add the lime juice at the very end of cooking or as a finishing element to preserve its volatile aromatic compounds and bright acidity.
Pair with a pinch of salt and a drizzle of high-quality olive oil to emulsify the flavors and coat the palate, enhancing the perception of freshness.

faq.q: How to store leftovers made with Lime and Onion?
faq.a: Store in an airtight glass container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. The acidity of the lime acts as a natural preservative, but the onion may continue to release moisture, so drain any excess liquid before serving to maintain texture.

For lime, use lemon juice or a splash of rice vinegar for acidity, though you will lose the distinct floral notes. For onion, try shallots for a milder, sweeter profile or green onions for a fresher, less pungent alternative.
